mcqs.question: When a scientist records the outcome of an experiment, how does using the results as evidence help make the investigation fair?

options.A: It allows the scientist to prove the hypothesis is always true.
options.B: It provides factual data that can be examined by others to support or refute conclusions.
options.C: It lets the scientist ignore any unexpected observations.
options.D: It replaces the need for a control group.

mcqs.answer: It provides factual data that can be examined by others to support or refute conclusions.
mcqs.explanation: Using results as evidence means the data are factual and can be shared with others. This allows the scientific community to evaluate whether the conclusions are justified. Options A, C and D describe misconceptions about evidence.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best shows that a student recognizes a limitation of their investigation?

options.A: I measured the temperature with a thermometer that was accurate to 0.1°C.
options.B: I could only test the plant growth for one week, so I cannot say what would happen over a longer period.
options.C: I used the same type of soil for all plants.
options.D: I repeated the experiment three times.

mcqs.answer: I could only test the plant growth for one week, so I cannot say what would happen over a longer period.
mcqs.explanation: Recognising a limitation means acknowledging what the investigation cannot tell us. Option B admits the short observation period limits the conclusion. Options A, C and D describe good practices, not limitations.

mcqs.question: What is the main purpose of conducting a scientific investigation?

options.A: To prove that the scientist’s idea is correct.
options.B: To explore a question and gather evidence that can answer it.
options.C: To collect as many facts as possible without a specific question.
options.D: To create a new invention immediately.

mcqs.answer: To explore a question and gather evidence that can answer it.
mcqs.explanation: The purpose of an investigation is to answer a specific question by collecting evidence. Option A confuses purpose with bias, C lacks focus, and D jumps to application rather than investigation.

mcqs.learning_point: Changing one relevant factor at a time where appropriate
mcqs.question: A student wants to find out how the amount of water affects the height of a bean plant. Which step follows the principle of changing one relevant factor at a time?

options.A: Use three different types of beans while keeping water amount the same.
options.B: Change the amount of water for each plant but keep the type of bean, soil, and sunlight the same.
options.C: Change both the amount of water and the type of soil together.
options.D: Keep all conditions the same and observe the plants for a week.

mcqs.answer: Change the amount of water for each plant but keep the type of bean, soil, and sunlight the same.
mcqs.explanation: Changing only the water amount isolates its effect, which is the core idea of changing one factor at a time. Options A and C change other variables, and D does not vary the factor of interest.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the best example of keeping other relevant conditions controlled during an experiment on the effect of sunlight on mold growth?

options.A: Placing some petri dishes in sunlight and others in darkness, while also using different types of food for the mold.
options.B: Using the same type of bread, same temperature, and same humidity for all dishes, but varying only the amount of sunlight each receives.
options.C: Changing both the amount of sunlight and the temperature for each dish.
options.D: Measuring mold growth only once at the end of the experiment.

mcqs.answer: Using the same type of bread, same temperature, and same humidity for all dishes, but varying only the amount of sunlight each receives.
mcqs.explanation: Controlling all other conditions ensures that any difference in mold growth is due to sunlight alone. Option A varies food, C varies two factors, and D does not address control.

mcqs.question: Riya measures the temperature of water every minute for five minutes while heating it. Why is making repeated observations important in this investigation?

options.A: It helps to confirm that the temperature reading is a one‑time accident.
options.B: It allows her to see how the temperature changes over time and detect any irregularities.
options.C: It lets her ignore any unexpected temperature spikes.
options.D: It proves that the thermometer is always correct.

mcqs.answer: It allows her to see how the temperature changes over time and detect any irregularities.
mcqs.explanation: Repeated observations give a pattern of change and help spot errors or unexpected trends. Options A, C, and D misinterpret the role of repeated measurements.

mcqs.question: Which statement shows a common misconception about recording results honestly?

options.A: I will write down the measurements exactly as I observed them, even if they don’t match my expectation.
options.B: If the results don’t support my hypothesis, I will change the numbers to make them look better.
options.C: I will keep a detailed notebook of each step of the experiment.
options.D: I will ask a friend to check my recorded data for errors.

mcqs.answer: If the results don’t support my hypothesis, I will change the numbers to make them look better.
mcqs.explanation: Altering data to fit a hypothesis is dishonest and undermines scientific integrity. Options A, C, and D describe honest practices.

mcqs.question: A class conducts an experiment to test which material conducts heat best. They record that a metal rod heats up faster than plastic. Which reasoning correctly explains why these results can be used as evidence?

options.A: Because the metal rod was longer, so it had more surface area to absorb heat.
options.B: Because the experiment was performed under the same conditions except for the material, so the difference in heating speed shows the material’s conductivity.
options.C: Because the students liked metal more than plastic.
options.D: Because the plastic rod was painted, affecting the result.

mcqs.answer: Because the experiment was performed under the same conditions except for the material, so the difference in heating speed shows the material’s conductivity.
mcqs.explanation: When all other variables are controlled, the observed difference can be attributed to the material itself, making the result valid evidence. Options A, C, and D introduce uncontrolled variables or irrelevant reasons.
